description.p: Use one keyboard and mouse across paired computers on your local network. Push the pointer through a screen edge or use a shortcut to switch machines, and take the clipboard with you.

On Wayland, the desktop controls input capture. Beamer can send input out when the pointer crosses an edge, but its shortcut only brings input back. It cannot hold an edge for a full-screen app, keep selected keys on the Linux computer while input is away, or draw crossing effects at the Linux screen edge.

On X11, Beamer can send and receive input across paired computers, including keyboard, pointer and clipboard. The Linux build has been tested on Fedora 44 with GNOME 50 under Wayland; X11 on real hardware and KDE Plasma have not been tested.

description.p: On Windows, a new setting, Control administrator windows, lets Beamer move the pointer and type in apps that run as administrator. It is off by default, asks for permission once, and applies only to that PC. When Windows blocks Beamer's input, the notice now names the app in front and appears once for each window, not on every switch, and the firewall check says when it needs administrator permission.

Scrolling a settings page no longer changes a slider or a drop-down list that the pointer stops over: a control takes the scroll wheel only after it is clicked or reached with the keyboard. When a Windows PC, another Mac or a Linux PC on X11 drives a Mac, holding a letter now opens the macOS accent menu in apps that offer it.

Explains on Wayland that the desktop controls pointer visibility while input is shared, and that Beamer cannot hide another application's idle pointer. Pointer hiding on macOS, Windows and X11 is unchanged.

Adds a Check for updates button to the Updates section on macOS, Windows and Linux. It works even when automatic checks are off, says when a check fails, and shows any newer version with a download link or Flatpak update instructions. Nothing downloads or installs automatically.
From this version, bug-fix patches no longer raise the update banner or menu alert unless they are marked important. They still appear on the Updates page and in manual checks.

Windows starts without an administrator prompt. The installer asks for permission separately to set up firewall rules, move existing Beamer startup tasks to normal rights and restart the GameInput service if present. Beamer can no longer control administrator windows or Windows permission prompts from another machine, no longer restarts GameInput while running, and its Firewall page now only checks the rules: run the installer again to repair them.
Fixes a crossing from Windows to a Mac with more than one display landing on the wrong display instead of the one set for that edge. Input from another machine now wakes a sleeping Mac display.

The Membrane, Sparks and Instrument crossing styles now follow the Size setting, and Light, Folio and Selvedge grow in every direction instead of only deeper. Switch effects such as Ring follow Size too. The largest Size is now 25% of the display's shorter side, up from 8% with a 144-point cap. The Design preview keeps the same zoom while Size changes, so it can crop larger marks.

Desktop machine rows have a Pin address switch: keep the address you chose, or turn it off to follow automatic address changes. On macOS, the Dock and menu bar controls sit higher on Overview, and the menu bar menu has a Show in Dock checkbox.

Fixes the pointer falling seconds behind when a 1000 Hz mouse bends, reverses or drags: once the link is behind, the pointer now goes straight to its latest position instead of replaying every step. Clicks, keys, scrolling and the clipboard still arrive in order around the motion.

Moves are sent at once while the other machine keeps up, and paced only once it falls behind. A settings file this version cannot read, such as one written by a newer Beamer, no longer crashes the window and is never overwritten.
Avoids repeatedly reading clipboard contents that cannot be shared and removes an unnecessary wait when returning with an empty clipboard. Failed clipboard reads can still retry.

Limits repeated Identify screens requests and leaves machines without an active desktop link out. Disabling update checks also clears the Mac menu's stale update action. Flatpak update actions consistently point to store update guidance. Windows input recovery clears stale modifiers after returning from the secure desktop.

The separate Windows portable package keeps its settings beside the executable and protects them with a passphrase. It needs no installation or administrator rights and does not change startup tasks or firewall rules. It cannot control elevated applications or the secure desktop. Discovery keeps installed and portable copies separate without duplicating replies sent through temporary network sockets.

Reduces mouse input building up on a slow receiver by reading ahead and combining waiting horizontal or vertical movement. Total travel and the order of buttons, keys and scrolling are preserved. Diagonal moves, reversals and axis changes stay separate to preserve crossing zones.

Improves clipboard reliability around switching machines, including brief retries when the clipboard is busy. Adds a visible notice for newer stable updates, with What's new and a per-version Dismiss button. Flatpak users get store update guidance. Linux builds now check GitHub for new versions too; turn off Check for updates in Settings to stop it. Nothing downloads or installs automatically.
Adds a Mouse only switch on macOS, Windows and Linux X11 to keep the keyboard on the machine you are using while sharing the mouse and clipboard. This switch is unavailable on Wayland.

Improves Windows-to-Linux accent handling by reading the foreground Windows app's layout, preserving printable AltGr output and trying Linux AltGr levels and supported single-accent dead-key sequences. Wayland still cannot type characters outside these supported layout paths.
Includes the missing library for generating pairing QR codes in Linux Flatpak builds. The README and bug-report form now list the Linux log locations.
Adds Identify screens on the Crossing page, showing numbers on local and directly linked desktop displays for three seconds. Machines on older versions are left out.
On Windows, Beamer no longer crashes at startup when the account name has an accented letter, such as É; thanks to kinowill for tracking it down.

While machines are linked, Beamer's log now summarises connection timings about every 30 seconds and tries to add a final summary when a connection ends: how long each machine spends queueing, sending, reading and applying input and scheduling its acknowledgement, and which addresses each connection uses. These lines hold times, counts and addresses only, not keys, text or pointer positions.

The Windows installer and Beamer.exe are now signed with a Certum code-signing certificate, so Windows shows the publisher's name; SmartScreen may still warn until the certificate builds a reputation. Nothing else changes from 1.5.7.
Keeps the address you chose for a machine after reconnects and restarts, instead of replacing it with a discovered or incoming one.
Carries the 1.5.5 audit fixes: Korean Han/Yeong and Hanja key repeat on X11, typed machine names on US-English systems, the Crossing shortcut tile subtitle, and the single-display map frame.
Adds layout profiles, shake to come home, resizable machine tiles on the Crossing map, and an Italian translation.
Fixes the shortcut leaving input stranded when it picked a machine that had just turned it away.
Adds pointer hiding on idle screens, idle takeover, per-screen crossing with contact-span matching, and Mac and Qt refresh improvements.
Adds the shared desk map, granular settings, dormant pairing repair and Linux crossing effects.
Fixes the Linux key-box hint and other issues found in the 1.5.0 release.
Adds Linux support and expands multi-computer support.
